items.t: Laparoscopic appendicectomy
items.c: Remember: In laparoscopic appendicectomy, follow the taenia coli to the caecal base to find the appendix, control the mesoappendix (appendicular artery) first, then ligate the base and divide it.

items.t: Fuller's bivalve metal tracheostomy tube
items.c: Remember: Fuller's tube = bivalve (two-bladed) metal tracheostomy tube, helpful for easy insertion in obese or short-necked patients and a deep trachea; Jackson's tube = metal with an inner tube.
items.a: Fuller's bivalve metal tracheostomy tube

items.t: Right inguinal hernia with an extended sac
items.c: Remember: inguinal hernias lie ABOVE and medial to the pubic tubercle (femoral hernias lie below and lateral to it); CT showing bowel or fat in a sac along the spermatic cord confirms the diagnosis and detects strangulation.
items.a: Right inguinal hernia with an extended sac

items.t: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
items.c: Remember: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck is the female equivalent of an encysted hydrocele of the cord, due to a patent processus vaginalis along the round ligament; treat with excision and high ligation of the sac.

items.t: Neurocysticercosis (intraventricular cysticercus cyst)
items.c: Remember: Intraventricular (fourth ventricle) cysticercus causes obstructive hydrocephalus.

items.t: Wolf forceps (Vrikamukha swastikayantra)
items.c: Remember: Sushruta's swastikayantra are 24 cross-shaped hinged forceps named after animal and bird faces (simha, vrika, krauncha, etc.), used mainly to extract foreign bodies.
items.a: Wolf forceps (Vrikamukha swastikayantra)
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Thyroid resection (goiter surgery) through a collar incision with a retractor system
items.c: Remember: Goiter surgery = collar (Kocher) incision, strap muscle retraction, identify the recurrent laryngeal nerve and preserve the parathyroids; frame retractors give hands-free exposure through small incisions.
items.a: Thyroid resection (goiter surgery) through a collar incision with a retractor system
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Split-thickness skin graft donor site
items.c: Remember: a split-thickness graft donor site is a clean, uniform partial-thickness wound with punctate bleeding points.
items.a: Split-thickness skin graft donor site

items.t: Nasal retractor (nasal speculum type)
items.c: Remember: a nasal retractor or speculum has small ball-tipped blades, a spring and a thumb screw.
items.a: Nasal retractor (nasal speculum type)

items.t: Hepatic cystic echinococcosis (hydatid cyst)
items.c: Remember: in hepatic hydatid disease, avoid spillage of cyst contents, which can cause anaphylaxis and secondary seeding.

items.t: Caecum after laparoscopic removal of the vermiform appendix
items.c: Remember: the three taeniae coli of the caecum converge at the base of the appendix, guiding the surgeon to it during laparoscopic appendicectomy; McBurney's point lies at the junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the line from the ASIS to the umbilicus.

items.t: Fibularis longus tendon
items.c: Remember: fibularis longus passes behind the lateral malleolus (superficial to brevis), grooves the cuboid, crosses the sole, and inserts on the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal base; it everts the foot and is supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.
items.a: Fibularis longus tendon

items.c: Remember: a trephine has a hollow, serrated circular crown on a shaft and cuts a disc of bone.

items.c: Remember: in laparoscopic cholecystectomy the gallbladder is a pale-bluish pear-shaped sac under the inferior liver edge; always achieve the critical view of safety before clipping.

items.t: Deaver retractor
items.c: Remember: Deaver retractor = broad, smooth, S-shaped handheld blade to hold back liver, bowel or viscera; Balfour = self-retaining abdominal frame; Richardson = short right-angled blade for the abdominal wall.

items.t: Hurd tonsil dissector and pillar retractor
items.c: Remember: Hurd dissector and pillar retractor is a double-ended instrument: spatulate end to dissect the tonsil capsule, angled blade to retract the anterior pillar in dissection tonsillectomy.

items.t: Microsurgical needle holder (Castroviejo-type)
items.c: Remember: Microsurgical needle holder = spring (looped) handle, pencil grip, fine jaws, often with a lock; gold handles mark fine microsurgical instruments (Castroviejo type).

items.t: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis
items.c: Remember: In laparoscopic cholecystectomy, achieve the Critical View of Safety (two and only two structures entering the gallbladder) before clipping the cystic duct and cystic artery, and always retrieve the gallbladder in a bag.
items.a: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis

items.t: Graily Hewitt's ordinary long-bladed obstetric forceps
items.c: Remember: Kielland = sliding lock, minimal pelvic curve, rotation.

items.c: Remember: a fasciotomy wound that cannot be closed primarily is covered temporarily (synthetic skin substitute, vessel loop shoelace or NPWT) and then closed late or skin grafted after the swelling resolves.
items.a: Surgery

items.t: Laparoscopic hysterectomy
items.c: Remember: In laparoscopic hysterectomy, the ureter lies beneath the uterine artery ('water under the bridge'), so skeletonize the vessels and keep cautery close to the uterus to avoid ureteric injury.
items.a: Laparoscopic hysterectomy
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Laparoscopic groin hernia repair
items.c: Remember: Three small port scars (umbilical + two lower abdominal) and no groin incision = laparoscopic (TAPP/TEP) groin hernia repair, with mesh in the preperitoneal space covering the myopectineal orifice.
items.a: Laparoscopic groin hernia repair

items.t: Obstetric forceps
items.c: Remember: obstetric forceps have 4 parts per branch (blade, shank, lock, handle), 2 curves (cephalic and pelvic) and fenestrated blades.
items.a: Obstetric forceps
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Chronic leg ulcer showing healing by pinch (Reverdin-type) skin grafts
items.c: Remember: pinch (Reverdin) grafts are small skin pieces placed on a clean granulating bed; each surviving graft becomes an island of epithelium that spreads outward and coalesces with others.
items.a: Chronic leg ulcer showing healing by pinch (Reverdin-type) skin grafts
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Weitlaner retractor
items.c: Remember: Weitlaner = scissor-handled, ratchet-locked, self-retaining retractor with 3 and 4 prongs for superficial wounds; Balfour = abdominal; Finochietto = thoracic.
items.a: Weitlaner retractor
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Vermiform appendix
items.c: Remember: the three taeniae coli converge at the base of the appendix, and this is the guide to finding it at surgery.
items.a: Vermiform appendix
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.c: Remember: Post-amputation pain out of proportion, bronze or dusky skin, hemorrhagic bullae, crepitus, and a foul serosanguinous discharge mean gas gangrene.
items.a: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.rn: Surgery

items.t: Submucous fibroid of the posterior uterine wall
items.c: Remember: a smooth, pale, firm, broad-based mass bulging into the cavity on hysteroscopy with menorrhagia and infertility is a submucous fibroid.
items.a: Submucous fibroid of the posterior uterine wall

items.t: Needle holder
items.c: Remember: a needle holder has short, stout, flat, cross-hatched jaws (often with a groove or tungsten carbide insert) and a locking ratchet.
items.a: Needle holder

items.t: Cheatle forceps
items.c: Remember: Cheatle forceps = long, angled, NON-ratcheted transfer forceps for lifting sterile items from drums.
items.a: Cheatle forceps

items.t: Retrieval of the appendix in an Endobag
items.c: Remember: In laparoscopic appendicectomy, always remove the appendix in an Endobag through the port to prevent port-site infection and tumour seeding.

items.t: Adhesions after appendectomy
items.c: Remember: Previous abdominal surgery (appendectomy, especially for perforation) is the commonest cause of adhesions, and adhesions are the commonest cause of small bowel obstruction in adults.

items.t: Left anterolateral (resuscitative) thoracotomy through the 4th or 5th intercostal space with a Finochietto rib retractor
items.c: Remember: Resuscitative thoracotomy is a left anterolateral incision in the 4th/5th intercostal space at the nipple level, and the Finochietto retractor handle points down toward the bed (axilla/bed side) so a clamshell extension remains possible.

items.t: Skin-grafting scissors
items.c: Remember: Skin-grafting scissors have fine, long, curved, pointed blades for atraumatic trimming of thin grafts; heavy blunt-tipped Mayo scissors cut fascia.
items.a: Skin-grafting scissors

items.t: Liston bone cutting forceps (curved)
items.c: Remember: Liston bone cutting forceps = long handles, spring, sharp cutting blades (straight or curved) used to trim bone ends, e.g., after amputation; Luer = nibbling cups.
items.a: Liston bone cutting forceps (curved)

items.t: Plain (uncuffed) tracheostomy tube
items.c: Remember: plain (uncuffed) tracheostomy tube = flange with tape slots, no cuff or pilot balloon.
items.a: Plain (uncuffed) tracheostomy tube

items.t: Deep plane facelift with SMAS elevation and fixation suture placement
items.c: Remember: The SMAS is the layer continuous with the platysma, parotid fascia and temporoparietal fascia; facelifts reposition it, and the facial nerve branches lie deep to it.
items.a: Deep plane facelift with SMAS elevation and fixation suture placement

items.t: Curved artery forceps (mosquito/Halsted type)
items.c: Remember: Artery forceps = ratcheted, box-lock, serrated, non-toothed jaws that clamp vessels; mosquito forceps are the smaller, finer version used in delicate ENT and paediatric surgery.
items.a: Curved artery forceps (mosquito/Halsted type)

items.t: Sponge holding forceps

items.t: Roman forceps with fine-toothed hollow jaws
items.c: Remember: Roman forceps have a scissor-type pivot (crossed arms) with fine-toothed hollow jaws to grip foreign bodies and tissue, unlike a speculum (valves), catheter (hollow tube) or lever (single shaft).
items.a: Roman forceps with fine-toothed hollow jaws

items.t: Displaced intra-articular distal radius fracture
items.c: Remember: Intra-articular distal radius fracture with articular step-off over 2 mm needs anatomical reduction and fixation to prevent post-traumatic arthritis; check radial height, inclination and volar tilt.

items.t: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) of the amputation stump
items.c: Remember: crepitus + pain out of proportion + dusky skin + foul serosanguinous discharge in a stump within 1-3 days = gas gangrene (Clostridium perfringens).

items.c: Remember: Single-incision laparoscopic cholecystectomy uses a multichannel umbilical port (e.g., TriPort); the gallbladder is extracted through the umbilicus, and the critical view of safety is mandatory before clipping.
